question: Let $A$ be any $3 \times 3$ skew symmetric matrix. Prove that $|A|=0$.
explanation:
For any $n \times n$ skew symmetric matrix,
$|A|=|A^T|=|-A|$.
$|-A| = (-1)^n|A|$
For $n=3$ (odd), $|-A| = -|A| \Rightarrow |A| = -|A| \implies |A|=0$.

options.A: Since $A$ is skew symmetric, $A^T=A$. Therefore $|A|=|A^T|=|A|$, so $|A|=1$.
options.B: Since $A$ is skew symmetric, $A^T=-A$. Hence $|A|=|A^T|=|-A|=(-1)^3|A|=-|A|$, so $2|A|=0$ and therefore $|A|=0$.
options.C: Since $A$ is skew symmetric, all diagonal elements are $1$. Hence the determinant of $A$ is always $0$.
options.D: Since $A$ is a $3 \times 3$ matrix, $|-A|=|A|$. Hence every skew symmetric matrix has determinant $1$.
